question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 7(1)/(3)years at the rate of 4.5% per annum is ₹6,270. What will be the amount payable on the same sum at the rate of 8.6% per annum simple interest in 11(1)/(2) years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest percentage for Case 1 = 4.5% × (22/3) = 33%.

Given, 33% of Principal = ₹6,270 ⇒ Principal = (6270 ÷ 33) × 100 = ₹19,000.

Effective interest percentage for Case 2 = 8.6% × (23/2) = 98.9%.

Total Amount percentage = 100% (Principal) + 98.9% (Interest) = 198.9%.

Amount payable = 198.9% of 19,000 = 198.9 × 190 = ₹37,791.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹37,791.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest in Case 1 (SI₁) = ₹6,270

Time in Case 1 (T₁) = 7 1/3 years = 22/3 years

Rate in Case 1 (R₁) = 4.5% per annum

Time in Case 2 (T₂) = 11 1/2 years = 23/2 years

Rate in Case 2 (R₂) = 8.6% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 
 Sum (P)
 
 

 

 
 

 

 
 
 Case 1: SI = ₹6,270
 R = 4.5%, T = 22/3 yrs
 
 
 Case 2: Amount = ?
 R = 8.6%, T = 23/2 yrs

**Calculations:**

Finding the principal (P) using Case 1:

⇒ SI₁ = (P × R₁ × T₁) ÷ 100

⇒ 6270 = (P × 4.5 × 22/3) ÷ 100

⇒ 6270 = (P × 1.5 × 22) ÷ 100

⇒ 6270 = (P × 33) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (6270 × 100) ÷ 33

⇒ P = 190 × 100 = ₹19,000

Finding the Simple Interest for Case 2 (SI₂):

⇒ SI₂ = (P × R₂ × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (19000 × 8.6 × 23/2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 190 × 4.3 × 23

⇒ SI₂ = 190 × 98.9 = ₹18,791

Total amount payable:

⇒ Amount = P + SI₂

⇒ Amount = 19000 + 18791 = ₹37,791

**∴ The correct answer is ₹37,791.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount accumulated on a principal under simple interest over time is directly calculated as A = P[1 + (R × T)/100].

Effective Interest Method

In Simple Interest, the effective interest percentage for `T` years at rate `R` is simply (R × T)%. This percentage value can directly be multiplied with the principal to find the total interest.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Unlike Simple Interest which is calculated strictly on the original principal throughout the term, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal along with the accumulated interest from the previous periods.
